---
title: "Optional research direction: Multiparameter persistence"
subtitle: "Optional extension beyond one ordered scale"
toc: true
---

Ordinary persistence follows one ordered parameter. Two axes on a plot do not
automatically define a multiparameter persistence module. Some constructions have
two choices that both create inclusions, such as neighbourhood scale and a
density threshold. Multiparameter persistence retains both directions rather
than collapsing one in advance.

## A genuine bifiltration

Give each point $x$ a codensity score $q(x)$, such as distance to its $k$th
nearest neighbour. Retain

$$X_\delta=\{x:q(x)\leq\delta\},$$

then build

$$K_{\delta,\varepsilon}=\operatorname{VR}_\varepsilon(X_\delta).$$

Increasing $\delta$ admits more points and increasing $\varepsilon$ admits
more simplices. Therefore

$$
(\delta,\varepsilon)\leq(\delta',\varepsilon')
\Longrightarrow
K_{\delta,\varepsilon}\subseteq K_{\delta',\varepsilon'}.
$$

The inclusions supply horizontal and vertical homology maps on the parameter
grid. A surface $\beta_1(\delta,\varepsilon)$ is one visible summary of this
two-parameter family.

## Why time needs care

Independent frames $X_t$ do not generally satisfy
$X_t\subseteq X_{t+1}$. A heat map with time and scale therefore need not be a
two-parameter module. Time can serve as a second ordered parameter when the
construction genuinely gives inclusions, for example when $X_t$ contains all
observations accumulated up to time $t$.

## What becomes difficult

One-parameter modules decompose into intervals under suitable conditions.
General multiparameter modules do not have an equally complete barcode
classification. Dimension functions, rank invariants, slices and other
summaries reveal selected aspects without completely determining the module.

The important distinction is between a plotted surface with
two axes and a module with two compatible families of maps. Representation
theory and decomposition results are specialist developments.
